A4_S3_D1: ^Narrator: Clara leads you through the dense trees and into a clearing. Nestled in the clearing is a homestead overlooking a sunlit meadow.
^Narrator: A meandering river heels the farm, shaded by trees. As you take in your surroundings, you notice dozens of cotton balls bouncing around, seemingly with a will of their own…
^Clara: In a way, they’re both. They're small but they're vital to our survival on this island. I love them to bits, even if they can be a handful.
^Clara: It used to be me and my mentor, Ada, but now it's just me!
^Narrator: One of the woolly critters is happily circling Clara’s feet.
^Clara: As you can see, they’re covered in a cotton-like, woolly coat, which we harvest to spin into textiles.
^Clara: It ends up growing back, so it doesnt hurt them at all!
^Noelle: (What can they make, I wonder…? Is it the same as the cotton plants from Dusk?)
^Noelle: How do you make these textiles?
^Clara: You know, I’m not sure exactly… That’s Rowan’s job — our head craftsman!
^Clara: You’ll meet him soon enough. Some of the arrivals from Noah's time specialised in making fine textiles. So they've adapted their customs to work with the resources here!
^Amelia: That includes the tapestries from the Viridi village, right? We saw a few of them.
^Clara: Yup, yup! Since you seem to be interested in them, would you like to help me shear their coats?
choiceanytips: ^Clara: Sometimes petting them can help to calm them down. Like this.
^Narrator: Clara demonstrates a circular patting motion.
choiceletsdoit: ^Narrator: You try to grab the closest creature to you. It immediately wriggles out of your arms and bounces away.
^Clara: Oh! They can be pretty mischievous, especially with strangers.
afterchoiceact4: ^Narrator: As soon as you begin patting the creature’s soft head, it stops trying to escape your arms. Clara passes you the shears and you relieve the cute critter of some of its wool.
^Clara: You got it! Let’s do five more each.
A4_S3_D2: ^Narrator: Inside the farmhouse, Clara prepares a quick pot of tea, mentioning that it’s from the Viridi.

^Clara: Their knowledge of the forest really is such a blessing! I think you’ve probably met her — Chione has taken up the mantle of studying plants after her master retired, and was the one to mix these packets of dried flowers and herbs.
^Narrator: Amelia leans forward from her chair, reading the label.
^Amelia: ‘Good for relaxation and calming the mind before sleep.’
^Clara: Normally I like the ones for sharpening the senses more, but since we have a fourth guest on the way…
^Narrator: Two knocks echo on the door.
^Narrator: Cillian introduces himself to you and Amelia, explaining that he was busy sorting out some business to do with the floods.
^Cillian: As Elder Silas might’ve informed, there are a couple of artifacts in our possession that might be of interest to you. And a certain box that we’ve never been able to open.
choiceforce: ^Cillian: Well… we didn’t want to damage it too much. And as it was made of metal, one can’t be sure if the item inside would survive such force, or even melting by fire.
choicemechanism: ^Cillian: The box is made of metal, and seems to contain a type of puzzle element with its key.
afterchoiceA4S3: ^Cillian: To this day, we’ve haven’t found information that reveals its purpose or technique, either, so we’re at a bit of a loss.
^Narrator: Since it’s never been opened before though, Cillian reassures you that there’s no pressure if you can’t figure it out. You can start tomorrow when you’re rested.
^Cillian: Since you were from an island of only humans… Is there anything you’d like to ask me in particular?
^Narrator: Truthfully, you could think of a million questions if you tried. But one thing stands out…
^Noelle: How did the Krakenfolk come about?
^Noelle: I’ve only heard that they appeared after Noah’s time… and while I may be one of them, my home island has never encountered such a transformation before.
^Noelle: (And of course, I have to be the first that gets thrown out.)
^Cillian: I suppose right after Noah’s encounter with the kraken would be the best place to start.
^Narrator: During the battle between kraken and crew, the Great Disaster’s blood was shed and flowed into the ocean.
^Narrator: Over time, this would spread far and wide — ultimately, it is impossible for living beings to not have consumed it in some form.

^Narrator: That is not the singular cause, however. Only humans — non-adapted ones — would be susceptible to transforming into a Krakenfolk. Which could be triggered if they ingested a certain metallic compound.
^Cillian: The compound is rare, however, and can only be found in the deep ocean.
^Cillian: Considering your descriptions, it seems like the chalice you drank from may have been contaminated by it in some way.
^Narrator: No way. Could it have been when your father went scavenging?
^Narrator: Your heart twists, and it starts becoming hard to breathe.
^Cillian: …There is no reversal for becoming a Krakenfolk.
^Cillian: But they do gain a variety of new abilities, far beyond the evolution of regular Thavma.
^Clara: Right! They have enhanced strength, can breathe underwater…
^Clara: I’ve heard that their hair can even glow, and that the most skilled can control their tentacles as separate limbs!
^Amelia: Much cooler than being a plain old human.
^Narrator: You laugh, appreciating their efforts to comfort you.
^Noelle: If those are all true, then I really should be putting those skills to use. Or learning them, at least.
^Cillian: The Ichthyos can help with that.
^Narrator: Cillian explains that whenever a new Krakenfolk came around, the Ichthyos would be the first to volunteer ‘training’ them.
^Clara: They can be a little energetic, but they mean well and protect the waters around Thavmia.
^Clara: It’s safe to say that their work and the Viridi’s go hand in hand.
^Amelia: I haven’t actually met the Ichthyos before. Only seen some in passing when they visited inland.
^Clara: Oh, that’s rare! Staying out of water for too long dries their skin, so they’re more inclined to the ocean, since rivers are, uh…
^Narrator: Their expressions tell you that despite this, some Icthyos might have tried.
^Noelle: I look forward to meeting them eventually.
^Cillian: Feel free to make yourself at home.
^Cillian: We’ve put up one of our tents in the village for you. It should be the same appearance as the one from the Viridi.
^Cillian: Well, that’s because… Our very own weaver, Rowan, handed them out to us as camping gear.
^Cillian: They’re prototypes for the tents he’s going to make in bulk for the caverns.
^Cillian: The yellow helps remind us of the sun, no?
^Cillain: Details like that are important when you’re shut into the mountains for days.
^Clara: We hope the guestroom will be to your liking!
^Narrator: As if on cue, your stomach rumbles. Clara chuckles.
^Clara: We can find something for that too.
A4_S3_D3: ^Clara: The village has a small dining hall where we have meals and events. You can go there for dinner and tomorrow for breakfast if you’d like!
^Clara: You might’ve noticed that the Viridi have small appetites? It’s because of their plant-like features. So long as they get enough sunlight, their energy gets reserved a bit.
^Clara: As for the Ichthyos and Krakenfolk, though…
^Clara: Dinners with them are always exciting.
A4_S3_Q1_ONGOING: ^Clara: Just go to each of the critters and repeat the process, five times!
A4_S3_Q1_COMPLETED: ^Narrator: Would you like to finish this quest?
CompleteQuestA4S3: ^Narrator: After collecting the wool, you end up tired and hungry, and so Clara invites you guys into the farmhouse for snacks.
^Amelia: What are you waiting for? Let’s go in!
